cell.label: Assess severity of attack (mild, moderate, or severe), then give nebulized or aerosol beta-2 agonist in multiple doses or continuously.
Arrange follow up; maintains response 60 minutes after last treatment; normal physical exam; consider oral steroids.
Discharge home; continue treatment with inhaled SABA; consider oral steroids; inhaled corticosteroid; patient education; schedule follow-up appt 1-4 weeks.
Consider admission to ward; oxygen; continue inhaled SABA + ipratropium bromide; oral or IV steroids; monitor vital signs, FEV1, SaO2.
PEF ≤50% predicted, pCO2 ≥42 mm Hg, drowsiness or confusion: admit to MICU; O2; inhaled SABA hourly or continuously; consider adjunctive treatment; consider intubation and mechanical ventilation.
Treat as for a poor response (above): admit to MICU.

footnotes.footnote: PEF, peak expiratory flow; SABA, short-acting beta agonist.
Adapted from the National Heart, Blood, and Lung Institute Expert Panel Report 3 (EPR 3): Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Asthma. NIH Publication no. 08-4051, 2007.
